# A narrowed option read in an operand of an assignment back to an option:
# `count = n + 1` under `n != null`. The assignment wanted an option, and the
# checker handed that want to the operator's operands, so the narrowed `n`
# was left an option and `+` was refused ("operator + not defined for
# option[int] and int"). An operator other than == and != takes the option's
# element instead. Each target wraps the sum back into the option.

sngl test --platform=none app.sngl
stdout 'ok +2 tests, 0 failures'
sngl test --platform=html app.sngl
stdout 'ok +2 tests, 0 failures'
sngl test --platform=bubbletea --language=go app.sngl
stdout 'ok +2 tests, 0 failures'
sngl test --platform=fyne --language=go app.sngl
stdout 'ok +2 tests, 0 failures'
sngl test --platform=gtk4 --language=go app.sngl
stdout 'ok +2 tests, 0 failures'
sngl test --platform=android --language=kotlin app.sngl
stdout 'ok +2 tests, 0 failures'

-- app.sngl --
import "sngl:test"
import ui "sngl:ui"

var count option[int] = 1

func bump() {
    var n = count
    if n != null {
        count = n + 1
    }
}

component main ui.node {
    var total option[int] = 10
    ui.button #add(text="add", @click {
        var t = total
        if t != null {
            total = t * 2 + 1
        }
    })
}

func testAPackageOptionTakesTheSum(t test.Test, c main) {
    bump()
    bump()
    t.assert(count == 3)
}

func testAComponentOptionTakesTheProduct(t test.Test, c main) {
    c.add.click()
    t.assert(c.total == 21)
}
